caseStudies.role: Design systems, frontend architecture, portfolio publishing
caseStudies.title: Unifying portfolio storytelling with Behance and drawing presence
caseStudies.challenge: The source archives contained strong design material, multilingual copy and drawing assets, but also duplicate builds and generated noise.
process: Separate visitor experience from internal operations
caseStudies.solution: A workspace with shared content, a Next.js production site, Vite preview, static fallback and Behance-ready portfolio records.
caseStudies.outcome: The site can communicate design quality with a stronger public gallery while preserving maintainable publishing paths.

caseStudies.title: Designing a calm interface for dense creative material
caseStudies.challenge: Portfolio archives, drawings and external profile links can become visually noisy and cognitively expensive.
process: Use restrained cards and direct labels
caseStudies.solution: A calm gallery architecture that summarizes Behance, drawings and service paths without dashboard overload.
caseStudies.outcome: Visitors can understand the creative range quickly, then move into a brief or external portfolio with less friction.

caseStudies.role: 3D art direction, motion governance, frontend performance
caseStudies.title: Making 3D motion feel cinematic without exhausting the interface
caseStudies.challenge: The site needed stronger 3D and motion, but the SEIS philosophy requires calm pacing, accessibility and thermal restraint.
caseStudies.solution: A two-scene Three.js system: a full-bleed cinematic hero and a smaller gallery showcase for drawings, works and Behance signals.
caseStudies.outcome: The experience feels more premium and memorable while staying testable on desktop and mobile.
